messages:
Sam: Quick sync — we should consolidate GPU triage into a single per-region health SLO/dashboard. Right now ECC, Xid, and flaky card signals live in different places and we end up chasing noise. Proposal: compute a per-card health score (0-100) using weighted signals and fire an alert if score < 60 for >15m. Thoughts?

Maria: +1. Will help routing to the right oncall. My initial weights idea: ECC (40), Xid (30), recent reboots (20), util/anomaly (10). But we must normalize by region baseline — eu-west has older cards. :eyes:

Kevin: I like the weighted approach but we need to gate noisy XIDs. Pattern: require both rate + increasing trend. Example PromQL to detect persistent XID activity (draft):

Kevin: ```promql
sum by (gpu_id)(rate(gpu_xid_errors_total[15m])) > 0.02 and
increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[1h]) > 3
```

Jen: Also include a short TTL for single-cause alerts so we don't replace cards for 1-off cosmic events. Suggested health math (pseudo):

Jen: ```
norm_ecc = min(1, ecc_count_24h / ecc_thresh)
norm_xid = min(1, xid_rate_1h / xid_thresh)
recent_reboots = min(1, reboots_24h / reboot_thresh)
health = 100 - round(100*(0.4*norm_ecc + 0.3*norm_xid + 0.2*recent_reboots + 0.1*util_anom))
```

Maria: We should persist both raw signals and the computed health score into a metric like gpu_health_score{region, gpu_id} so dashboards and alerts are consistent. Grafana can then show heatmaps and top-k.

infra-bot: Auto-report: last 24h top XID sources: region=us-west, gpu_pool=g4a, gpu_id=nv-42 (12 XID events).

Leo-bot: Dashboard layout suggestion — left column: region overview heatmap (avg health per rack), center: top-10 worst GPUs, right: recent reboots & flaky-card timeline. Include a panel for "drain impact" estimate (how many pods would be rescheduled).

Sam: Good. For alerts, we should group by region and severity:
- P1: health < 40 for >10m -> immediate page & automated canary drain in dedicated pools.
- P2: health 40-60 for >30m -> ticket + oncall review.
- P3: health 60-80 -> monitor, run elevated telemetry.

Kevin: Example alert rule (Grafana/Prometheus style):

Kevin: ```yaml
alert: GPUHealthCritical
expr: avg_over_time(gpu_health_score{region="${region}"}[15m]) < 40
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "GPU health critical in $region ({{ $labels.gpu_id }})"
```

Jen: Runbook stub:
1) Check node metrics (ECC, XID, temp).
2) If health < 40 and reboots >1 -> cordon + drain: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
3) Replace card / open HW ticket if persistent after replacement.
4) Document vendor serial + batch in ticket.

Maria: We need a canary rollout of the alerting thresholds. I'd like to start with eu-west small fleet for 2 weeks, observe false positives. I'll create a dashboard snapshot and a short playbook.

Sam: Important cost note: proactive card replacements add CAPEX/OPEX. Kevin can you run a quick estimate of extra replacements per year for thresholds at 60 vs 40? We can quantify replacement cost vs expected downtime savings.

Kevin: Yep — rough calc: at threshold 60 we'd flag ~2.4% of fleet/year -> ~90 cards/year; at 40 it's ~0.8% -> ~30 cards/year. Need exact fleet size & current failure rate to refine.

Jen: One more ops thing — tie alerts to job routing: dedicated pools should auto-fallback to compatible instances before draining. Otherwise user traffic sees latency spikes.

Sam: Action items: Maria to draft dashboard + gpu_health_score metric + example alerts, Kevin to run cost/false-positive simulation, Jen to expand runbook steps and add drain automation guardrails. I'll schedule a 30m sync next Tue to review the canary plan. :+1:

Maria: On it — I'll post a dashboard link and snapshot here when ready. :rocket:

infra-bot: Noted owners: Maria (dashboard), Kevin (cost sim), Jen (runbook). Canary target: eu-west-1 100 GPUs, start 2024-11-01.

Kevin: Quick note on telemetry retention — keep raw error counters for 90d to analyze regressions, but pre-aggregate 1m -> 5m for long-term to save TSDB space.

Sam: Thanks all. If anyone sees obvious gaps call them out here. Otherwise I'll put the draft agenda in calendar.
